name: Mountains
overview: Scripture portrays mountains as significant landmarks where God's providence and judgment are revealed. The flood narrative shows mountains submerged under waters, yet the ark finds rest upon the mountains of Ararat, symbolizing divine preservation (Genesis 7:19-20; 8:4). Mountains serve as places of refuge and divine encounters, as seen when kings fled to them for safety (Genesis 14:10) and when Abraham was instructed to offer Isaac on a mountain in Moriah (Genesis 22:2). They also mark geographical and spiritual boundaries, such as Mount Seir and other regions, highlighting their importance in God's unfolding plan (Genesis 14:6).
